steps.text: run the totality oracles being refuted in one batched run confirmed with run --each (run --invariant <name>... --each), and see each green batched and alone
steps.leaves: run record for the bullets, pass; per-test run record, pass

steps.text: stage the smallest break that changes the behavior the bullet claims, not the strings the detector reads; read the diff to confirm the edit touched only the lines you meant
refute <component>/<name> --broke "<what you changed>"; the detector fails on its own assertion, not by a hang, a kill, a timeout, or what an earlier test left behind
steps.leaves: run record for the bullet, refutation red

steps.text: restore the source byte for byte: from HEAD when the code under test is committed, and from a copy taken before the break when it is not
steps.leaves: the file matches its state before the break (git diff against HEAD, or cmp against the copy)

steps.text: run them again in one batched run confirmed with run --each, and see each green batched and alone
steps.leaves: run record for the bullets, pass; per-test run record, pass

steps.text: when the red did not come from the break, record a decision that this refutation does not count and refute again; the run store is append-only, so the correction is a later record

pitfalls: a sed matched two lines, so the test hung and went red only when it was killed (d-828ddc83)
a substring detector passed an unconditional early return that kept every expected string (df-c40bb904, x-429ed176)
the red came from the selected test depending on what earlier tests appended, not from the break (d-c4be0b1a, df-9e673484)
a self-asserted refuted: line read as witnessed, and an automatic refutation proved the instrument reports a site, not that the classifier calls it a bypass (df-b9b2711b, df-87881a8d)
a break that turns a test red when the via does not test the claim refutes nothing; record unable instead (u-2e6ee400)

1.because: the first bullet was refuted before the batched and alone run; the run followed at once, before the other four breaks

6.evidence: two breaks first passed (the probe sorted first; a fixture with no git listing); neither counted, the tests were strengthened and each refuted again

chose: A language the config declares must also be named in the language key, which orders it among the project's languages
over: a declared language joining the project's languages by being declared
because: naming it is the one place the project orders its languages and picks the primary; a declaration nothing names would be read by nothing, so it is refused with the language list to write rather than added in an order the project never chose

chose: A declared language's adapter earns reference-choked and no rung above it
over: a declared visibility rule (a regex for an exported declaration) that earns visibility-choked
because: the language server protocol says nothing about visibility, and a rule the project writes about its own language would credit the compiler with a refusal Coherence never saw; layer 2 (adapter modules) is where a project that knows its language's visibility rules can earn the rung, with the refusal witnessed
binding: none: this session owns no active work order

chose: A declared language's refutation stages the config's refute template, and with none it is not run
over: a default template guessed per language, such as import {name} from {file}
because: a reference is spelled differently in every language, and a guessed template that the server does not read as a reference would make every chokepoint read not run for a reason no one wrote; the project names how its language spells one, and without it the honest verdict is not run, never pass
binding: none: this session owns no active work order

chose: Every reading names a declared language as not read, with one shared reason
over: scanning a declared language's text with the nearest built-in's rules
because: the readings' scans are per-language syntax tables; reading Swift as TypeScript would draw false declarations and imports, and a reading must say what it skipped (languages-read.ts)

chose: A single language string that names no known language is refused
over: falling back to TypeScript, as a single unknown string did
because: with languages declarable, an unknown name is most often a typo or a language declared under another name; falling back to TypeScript read a project in the wrong language without a word

chose: config.languages stays the built-in languages, and config.enforced lists every language a check may be written in
because: every reading types config.languages as built-ins and dispatches on them through exhaustive per-language tables (#116); keeping them built-in leaves those tables exhaustive, while enforcement, the one path that reads a declared language, reads enforced

chose: A document the generic adapter opens carries the declared language's name as its language id
over: a languageId key in the declaration
because: servers key their language ids by the names a language is commonly declared under (swift, go, kotlin), and typescript-language-server answered a document under an unknown id as it would its own; a separate key can be added when a server needs one
